_metadata.description: Chemical properties database for PFD simulator
sources: Poling, Prausnitz, O'Connell - Properties of Gases and Liquids

units.property_correlations: portable equation definitions with per-entry units_note

fusion_transitions.source: Emel'yanenko et al., Russian Journal of Physical Chemistry A 84 (2010) 1491-1497
fusion_transitions.comment: Measured with a PerkinElmer DSC-2C calibrated against high-purity indium; uncertainty is +/-0.2 kJ/mol. The same paper reports 14.7 +/- 0.2 kJ/mol after extrapolation to 298.15 K.

melting_transitions.source: Emel'yanenko et al., Russian Journal of Physical Chemistry A 84 (2010) 1491-1497
melting_transitions.comment: Measured melting temperature; uncertainty is +/-0.5 K.

rhol.quality_note: Single reported liquid-density datum at 20 degC; this is a point value, not a temperature-dependent density fit.

Psat.quality_note: Experimental transpiration correlation; portable polynomial is a numerical refit of the paper's published equation with maximum relative pressure error below 3e-8 over the declared range.
Psat.source: Emel'yanenko et al., Russian Journal of Physical Chemistry A 84 (2010) 1491-1497, doi:10.1134/S0036024410090074; refit of ln(p/Pa)=297.2/R-87581.1/(R*T)-(62.0/R)*ln(T/298.15)

Hvap.quality_note: Linear temperature relation implied by the paper's tabulated vaporization enthalpies and adopted constant liquid-to-gas heat-capacity difference of 62.0 J/mol/K. The 333.8-368.4 K portion is supported by transpiration measurements; 298.15-333.8 K is the authors' extrapolation.
Hvap.source: Emel'yanenko et al., Russian Journal of Physical Chemistry A 84 (2010) 1491-1497, doi:10.1134/S0036024410090074; Hvap(T)=69.1-0.0620*(T-298.15) kJ/mol

Cpg.quality_note: Degree-5 least-squares fit in ln(Cp) to the paper's calculated ideal-gas heat capacities. Maximum tabulated-point relative error is 0.619%, MAPE is 0.139%, and RMS absolute error is 0.180 J/mol/K. These source values are molecular/statistical-mechanical results, not direct calorimetric measurements.
Cpg.source: Emel'yanenko et al., Russian Journal of Physical Chemistry A 84 (2010) 1491-1497, doi:10.1134/S0036024410090074; exponential polynomial refit of Table 5

sample.starting_material: Alfa Aesar dehydrated S-lactic acid, stated purity >98%

combustion.method: modified V-08MA isothermal-shell bomb calorimeter calibrated with NIST SRM 39j benzoic acid

Hcomb_gross.notes: Table 3 value at 298.15 K. The abstract instead prints -1337.9 +/-0.8 kJ/mol; the internally used result is -1338.4 +/-0.6 kJ/mol.

Hf_solid.notes: Crystalline standard formation enthalpy at 298.15 K, +/-0.7 kJ/mol. The abstract instead prints -700.1 +/-0.9 kJ/mol; Table 3 and Results give -699.7 +/-0.7 kJ/mol.

Hf_liquid.notes: Metastable-liquid value at 298.15 K derived as Hf_solid + Hfus(298.15 K) = -699.7 + 14.7 kJ/mol.

Hf.notes: Ideal-gas standard formation enthalpy at 298.15 K from the measured crystalline formation enthalpy and phase-change enthalpies, +/-1.3 kJ/mol.

Gf.notes: Ideal-gas standard Gibbs formation energy at 298.15 K from Table 5; calculated, not directly measured.

S.notes: Ideal-gas standard molar entropy at 298.15 K; calculated from conformer, molecular, and spectral data rather than directly measured.

Tb.notes: Low-confidence normal-boiling estimate of 232 degC (505.2 K; Clausius-Clapeyron and Ambrose-Walton); not an experimental hard anchor.

Hfus.notes: Measured at Tm=330.4 K, +/-0.2 kJ/mol; the extrapolated 298.15 K value is 14.7 +/-0.2 kJ/mol.

Hsub.notes: At 298.15 K, Hsub = Hfus + Hvap = 83.8 +/-1.0 kJ/mol.

dataset.notes: S-(+)-lactic acid property card. Combustion, vapor pressure, fusion, purity, and moisture are experimental; ideal-gas functions and conformer results are calculated. No normal boiling point or true critical constants are reported.

dataset.source: NIST scalar properties and heat-of-vaporization fit + J. Chem. Eng. Data 2017 density/viscosity + local Antoine refit
dataset.notes: Cp_coeffs, Hf, Hfus, Vc, S, and Hvap(T) from NIST; scalar Hvap is the normal-boiling value from the NIST fit; Gf derived from Hf and S using graphite C and H2 standard entropies at 298.15 K; density and viscosity from J. Chem. Eng. Data 2017, 62, 3, 1146-1152; Antoine A adjusted to match Psat=18.0 kPa at 17 C and Psat=1 atm near stored Tb.

Psat.selected_model: A-F refit of non-extrapolated nitric acid saturation pressures
Psat.quality_note: Unconstrained ln(P/bar) fit to all 17 source points from 231.55 K through 376.1 K; MARD 9.6e-8%, maximum relative error 3.5e-7%; extrapolated points above 376.1 K excluded
Psat.source: Wang et al., Fluid Phase Equilibria 407 (2016) 105-116, Table 3 extended Antoine from Aspen Plus databank; fit restricted through 376.1 K

Cpl.quality_note: Critically evaluated review correlation; fits Forsythe-Giauque liquid Cp table within 0.05%
Cpl.units_note: Cp in J/mol/K; x=(T-298.15 K)/100; converted from Cp(cal/mol/K)=25.64+1.427e-2*T-4.090e-5*T^2
Cpl.source: Stern, Mullhaupt, and Kay, Chem. Rev. 1960, The Physicochemical Properties of Pure Nitric Acid

Cpg.quality_note: Critically evaluated review correlation; fits Palm-Kilpatrick ideal-gas thermodynamic table within 0.1%
Cpg.units_note: Cp in J/mol/K; x=(T-298.15 K)/100; converted from Cp(cal/mol/K)=2.88+4.047e-2*T-2.407e-5*T^2

Hvap.source: Stern, Mullhaupt, and Kay, Chem. Rev. 1960, The Physicochemical Properties of Pure Nitric Acid

rhol.units_note: rho in kg/m^3; x = (T - 298.15 K)/100; degree-2 fit
rhol.source: Mercury liquid density: reference tables (0-250 C) + high-temperature data (691-979 K)

mul.units_note: ln(mu[Pa.s]) = A + B/T + C*ln(T); Arrhenius-with-log (DIPPR 101, D=0)
mul.source: Mercury liquid dynamic viscosity: high-quality data (250-500 K) + dynamic measurements (691-979 K)

Cpg.units_note: Shomate: Cp[J/mol/K] = A + B*t + C*t^2 + D*t^3 + E/t^2, t = T/1000; monatomic vapor near 5/2 R
Cpg.source: NIST Chemistry WebBook, Shomate equation for Hg(g)

Cpl.units_note: Cp in J/mol/K; x = (T - 298.15 K)/100; degree-2 fit
Cpl.source: Engineering Toolbox mercury liquid heat capacity, 250-500 K

Hvap.units_note: DIPPR 106: Hvap[kJ/mol] = A*(1-Tr)^(B + C*Tr + D*Tr^2), Tr = T/Tc; liquid range only (Tm to Tb), must NOT be extrapolated toward Tc (fit does not close there)
Hvap.source: Clausius-Clapeyron from the curated Hg Psat correlation (ideal-gas dZ); consistent with measured Hvap(Tb)=59.11 to 0.4% and Hf(Hg,g) at 298 K to 0.03%

dataset.source: Curated mercury property card (PFDSim) + Huber-Laesecke-Friend 2006 Psat
dataset.notes: Monatomic liquid metal; standard state is liquid (Hf_liquid=Gf_liquid=0); gas-phase Hf/Gf/S are formation values. Gas-phase Cp is the NIST Shomate portable fit (Cpg, above Tb); liquid Cp is a poly_x fit (Cpl, 250-500 K).
